en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on the Buddhas, 4. The Question on Seeing the Dhamma "Venerable sir," said King Milinda, "it was said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, it is through seeing the Dhamma that one sees me; it is through seeing me that one sees the Dhamma. Now, venerable sir, how does one see the Dhamma? And how does one see the Tathāgata? "It is, great king, through the Four Noble Truths that one sees the Dhamma; and it is through the Four Noble Truths that one sees the Tathāgata. "But, venerable sir, what is the Dhamma? And what is the Tathāgata? "The Dhamma, great king, is the Four Noble Truths: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the way leading to the cessation of suffering. And the Tathāgata, great king, is the one who has fully awakened to these Four Noble Truths, who has realized them, who has penetrated them, who has mastered them, and who has emerged from them. "But, venerable sir, how does one see the Dhamma? And how does one see the Tathāgata? "When, great king, a noble disciple sees with right wisdom as it really is: 'This is suffering,' he sees the Dhamma. When he sees the Dhamma, he sees the Tathāgata. When he sees with right wisdom as it really is: 'This is the origin of suffering,' he sees the Dhamma. When he sees the Dhamma, he sees the Tathāgata. When he sees with right wisdom as it really is: 'This is the cessation of suffering,' he sees the Dhamma. When he sees the Dhamma, he sees the Tathāgata. When he sees with right wisdom as it really is: 'This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,' he sees the Dhamma. When he sees the Dhamma, he sees the Tathāgata. It is in this way, great king, that one sees the Dhamma; and it is in this way that one sees the Tathāgata. "Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! Well explained, venerable Nāgasena! It is so, venerable Nāgasena! It is exactly so, venerable Nāgasena!"
"Venerable Nāgasena, has the Dhamma been seen by you?
"By the eye of the Buddha, Great King, and according to the Buddha's ordinance, disciples must conduct themselves for as long as life lasts."
Thus ends the fourth dilemma: On the Vision of the Dhamma.
